    1. installIfAvailable(ChaosRuntime)

Class JfrIntegration

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.bootstrap.jfr.JfrIntegration
@Internal public final class JfrIntegration extends Object
Entry point for the optional JFR integration layer.

Calling installIfAvailable(ChaosRuntime) is safe on any JVM. When JFR is not accessible (stripped JRE, disabled module), the method returns immediately without registering anything. When JFR is available, a JfrChaosEventSink is instantiated and registered as a lifecycle ChaosEventListener (ChaosRuntime.addLifecycleListener(ChaosEventListener)): it wires chaos events to Flight Recorder, and, since it never reads SKIPPED, a skipped call builds no event for it. It listens whether or not a recording runs, so the snapshot's total counts every application since the start; ChaosRuntime.close() closes it.

This class deliberately avoids loading jdk.jfr.* classes at its own load time — those are only referenced inside installJfr, which is only called after the probe succeeds.

  • Method Details

    • installIfAvailable

      public static void installIfAvailable(ChaosRuntime runtime)
      Probes JFR availability and, if present, installs a JfrChaosEventSink into runtime. The sink registers a periodic stressor snapshot hook and bridges lifecycle/applied events to JFR.

      This method is idempotent across multiple calls on the same runtime only in the sense that each call will install an additional sink. Callers (e.g., ChaosAgentBootstrap) must ensure it is called exactly once per runtime lifetime.

      Parameters:
      runtime - the runtime into which the JFR sink is installed
